title: Agentic GraphRAG: AI’s Logical Edge — Stephen Chin, Neo4j
talk_summary: Stephen Chin pitches GraphRAG as a way to reduce LLM hallucinations by using vector search to find seed nodes and graph traversal to pull related context, plus MCP tools and graph memory. The concrete mechanisms are hybrid retrieval, relevance filtering/ranking, and decoupling tools via MCP; most claims are vendor examples without controlled evals.

takeaways.what_they_do: Embed the question, vector-search to find seed nodes, then traverse graph relationships to pull related nodes as context instead of relying on similarity alone.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you do a vector search and then you use that to pull back related nodes in graph context

takeaways.what_they_do: Pre/post-filter vector results and bubble the most relevant items to the top of the prompt because LLMs attend mostly to the top of long contexts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: pre and post filtering of vector results to bubble things which are more relevant to the top of the context

takeaways.what_they_do: Store agent memory as a graph of entities/relationships so retrieval can follow associations rather than only vector similarity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: memory to your agents, which is graph-based and matches the way LM want to store, communicate, and retrieve information

takeaways.what_they_do: Expose tools/data through MCP servers so agents call standardized tools instead of a monolithic runtime with hard-coded integrations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use MCP as your tools where your agents are talking to them

takeaways.what_they_do: Use vector search plus graph context for critical retrieval; LLM-generated Cypher is unreliable for some cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: generation of cipher by LLMs is not as good as you need it for some cases
